content:
ashok: Quick thread — I've been digging into fragmentation patterns when we allocate small vector tiles for quantized model shards (3x/4x wide tiles). The common case: lots of sub-32KB allocations end up scattering across NUMA nodes and cause host staging thrash. Thinking about two complementary heuristics: 1) tile-coalesce-on-alloc (try to prefer contiguous tile windows) and 2) NUMA-aware soft-reserve (pre-pin small hot pools per NUMA with cheap eviction).
maria: Curious — how does this interact with our prefix/KV caching? If we coalesce aggressively we might increase tail latency for cold prefixes.
ashok: typo — meant ashok :)
ashok: Good call. Coalescing should be adaptive: only coalesce when hotness score > threshold and expected lifetime > X ms. For cold prefixes, fall back to scatter allocation.
liam: What about page size choice? We currently use 4K pages by default; switching hot pools to 2M hugepages fixes TLB pressure but increases internal fragmentation for small tiles. Tradeoff?
sofia: Hugepages helped on sequence-heavy workloads (reduced p-faults), but for tiny tile workloads they waste VRAM/host RAM. Maybe hybrid: hugepages for contiguous large allocations, 4K for small tiles, with an allocator that can aggregate small tiles into a 2M backing when density high.
maria: That aggregation sounds complex. Could we instead use a shadow-backing technique: keep small tiles in a packed host slab and expose contiguous GPU mappings via scatter-gather lists, then defragment by migrating hot slabs?
ashok: That's basically what I mean by tile-coalesce-on-alloc except with a migration plan. We should design an API for the runtime allocator with three primitives: reserve_hint(size, hotness), commit(reservation_id), and migrate(reservation_id, target_numa). Simple example:
```
// pseudocode
res = reserve_hint(24k, hotness=0.8)
if (res.succeeded) commit(res)
// later
migrate(res, numa=0) // move backing to node 0's pinned hot-pool
```
liam: API looks fine. Who owns migration semantics? Runtime or model shard loader? Need clear boundary. If runtime handles migration it can use telemetry to decide; if loader handles it we give users more control.
sofia: I'd prefer runtime-managed with opt-out. Most users don't want to handle NUMA. Expose telemetry and knobs but make default automatic.
maria: Telemetry requirement: we need short-window hotness, allocation lifetime histogram, and fragmentation heatmap per NUMA. Without that we can't tune thresholds.
infra-bot: Deploy note: telemetry pipeline can handle extra dimensions but will need a new roll of the ingestion schema (fragmentation_heatmap, tile_hotness). Expect slight cost bump.
ashok: Implementation plan sketch: (1) add per-NUMA hot pools with soft-reserve counters, (2) implement reserve_hint/commit/migrate API, (3) defragment background worker that compacts when hot-pool occupancy > 70% and migration ROI > cost_threshold, (4) add telemetry dimensions. Timeline: 2 sprints for proof-of-concept, 1 sprint for perf runs.
sofia: Can we avoid synchronous migration during inference? Need non-blocking move that tolerates in-flight requests. Use copy-on-write mapping + atomic pointer swap to KV cache entry.
ashok: Yes — migration should be bump-pointer swap after mirroring pages and validating checksums. Runtime must maintain dual mappings until all inflight users are drained.
liam: One last nit: eviction policy for soft-reserve pools should be fairness-aware across tenants. Consider lease epoch to avoid starve-reclaim loops.
maria: Agree. Also add a debug tool that prints per-alloc lineage: allocator-id, reserve-time, migrate-count, current-numa, hotness_score. That will help tune heuristics.
sofia: I'll draft a follow-up RFC with the API sketch + state machine for migrate/commit/evict and the telemetry schema.
ashok: Thanks. If anyone has objections to runtime defaulting to auto-NUMA and auto-coalesce, speak now. Otherwise I'll start the PoC. :thumbsup:
